([[Greenfield, Wisconsin]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 13 | draft_team = [[Miami Heat]] | career_start = 2019 | years1 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Miami Heat]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Star]] ({{nasg|2025}}) * [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] ({{nbay|2021|end}}) * [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2019|end}}) * [[NBA Three-Point Contest]] champion ({{nasg|2025}}) * Second-team [[List of All-SEC men's basketball teams|All-SEC]] (2019) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Newcomer of the Year]] (2019) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2019) | team2 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years2 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present }} '''Tyler Christopher Herro''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ||h|iː|r|oʊ}} {{respell|HEE|roh}};{{cite AV media |title=DRAKE Sent Tyler Herro These Kicks! Inside The Kentucky Guard's Sneaker Closet |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AlWS4C-8csg?si=BuvDxIfcFESJSmaT&t=15 |time=00:00:15 |publisher=[[Overtime (sports network)|Overtime]] |via=[[YouTube]] |date=1 August 2018 }} born January 20, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Herro was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 13th overall pick. With the Heat, Herro was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2020 and reached the [[2020 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in 2020 and 2023. He was named the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] in 2022 and was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] in 2025. Herro has played both [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] at the professional level. ==Early life== Herro was born in [[Milwaukee|Milwaukee, Wisconsin]], and graduated from [[Whitnall High School]] in [[Greenfield, Wisconsin]].{{Cite web |title=Tyler Herro, Kentucky Wildcats, Shooting Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Tyler-Herro-85253 |access-date=December 16, 2023 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}} In his senior season, he was named to the First Team All-State as he averaged 32.9 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 3.3 steals per game; his field goal percentage was over 50 and his three-point shooting percentage was 43.5. He scored more than 2,000 points in his high school career.{{cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6788|title=Tyler Herro - Men's Basketball|work=University of Kentucky Athletics|date=June 6, 2018 |access-date=September 2, 2019}} In high school, Herro received scholarship offers from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], [[Marquette University]], [[DePaul University]], [[Oregon State University]], and [[Arizona State University]]. He committed to play for the [[University of Wisconsin]] after visiting the Madison campus many times.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=September 12, 2016 |title=ESPN 60 junior guard Tyler Herro commits to Wisconsin |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/17532684 |access-date=September 8, 2020}} The commitment to the University of Wisconsin–Madison program was made before his junior year of high school in September 2016. In 2017 [[University of Kentucky]] coach [[John Calipari]] came to the Whitnall High School gymnasium to see Herro play in person. Herro then de-committed from Wisconsin on October 17, 2017. When Herro was no longer committed to play for Madison, he was recruited by the [[University of Kansas]] and [[University of Kentucky]]. Calipari offered Herro a scholarship on October 31, 2017. Herro then visited the Kentucky campus and decided to play for Kentucky.{{cite news |last=Page |first=Fletcher |date=November 29, 2017 |title=How Tyler Herro went from a Wisconsin commit to Kentucky-bound in 28 days |publisher=USA HSS |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/how-tyler-herro-went-from-a-wisconsin-commit-to-kentucky-bound-in-28-days |access-date=September 8, 2020}} Herro signed his letter of intent with Kentucky on November 14, 2017.{{cite news |last=Finkelstein |first=Adam |date=November 15, 2017 |title=Scout's Take: ESPN 100 SG Tyler Herro signs with Kentucky |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/insider/post/_/id/119887 |access-date=September 8, 2020}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Tyler Herro | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Greenfield, WI]] | highschool = [[Whitnall High School|Whitnall]] (WI) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 193 | 40 = | commitdate = November 14, 2017 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 89 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Kentucky 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Kentucky Wildcats Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = kentucky | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 96 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 36 | 247 overall = 38 | espn overall = 30 | accessdate = June 4, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his one year at Kentucky, Herro averaged 14.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists as the only player to start in all 37 games for the Wildcats. On February 27, 2019, he scored a collegiate career-high 29 points, making 9 of 10 field goals and all of 6 free throws, to lead the Wildcats to a comeback victory over the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]], 70–66.{{cite web|last=Taylor|first=Keith|date=February 27, 2019|title=Tyler Herro steps up to lead Wildcats to comeback win in close call against Razorbacks Tuesday night|url=https://www.nkytribune.com/2019/02/tyler-herro-steps-up-to-lead-wildcats-to-comeback-win-in-close-call-against-razorbacks-tuesday-night/|access-date=November 5, 2019|website=Northern Kentucky Tribune}} Among other distinctions earned, he was named an All-Freshman First Team selection by ''[[Basketball Times]]'' as well as the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Southeastern Conference Rookie of the Year]] by the [[Associated Press]]. On April 12, 2019, Herro declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility and hiring an agent. He was listed as a mid-first-round selection in most mock drafts.{{Cite web |date=April 12, 2019 |title=Tyler Herro declares for NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/04/12/tyler-herro-declares-for-nba-draft/ |access-date=December 16, 2023 |website=collegebasketball.nbcsports.com}} == Professional career == === Miami Heat (2019–2026) === On June 20, 2019, Herro was selected by the [[Miami Heat]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Tjarks |first=Jonathan |date=June 20, 2019 |title=Grading the 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.theringer.com/nba-draft/2019/6/20/18693649/2019-nba-draft-grades-zion-williamson |access-date=June 22, 2019 |website=The Ringer}} On July 10, the Heat announced that they had signed Herro.{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2019 |title=HEAT Signs Tyler Herro |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-tyler-herro-190710 |access-date=July 10, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} ==== 2019–2021: Rookie season and first Finals appearance ==== On October 23, he made his NBA debut, starting in a 120–101 victory over the [[2019–20 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]] and finishing the season-opener with 14 points to go along with 8 rebounds, 2 steals and an assist.{{cite web |date=October 23, 2019 |title=Butler misses Miami debut, Heat beat Grizzlies 120-101 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160629 |access-date=October 23, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}} In his fourth game (and first non-start), Herro scored a career-high 29 points on October 29 in a 112–97 win over the [[2019–20 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |date=October 29, 2019 |title=Butler makes his Miami debut, Heat top Hawks 112-97 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160694 |access-date=December 11, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}} Herro was due to play in the Rising Stars game during the All-Star Weekend in 2020, but was ruled out due to an ankle injury. On August 12, 2020, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 116–115 loss to the [[2019–20 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=August 12, 2020 |title=Heat's Tyler Herro erupted for a career-high 30 points vs. Thunder |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/08/12/tyler-herro-miami-heat-career-high-okc-thunder-highlights/ |access-date=December 29, 2021 |website=USA Today}} When the Heat defeated the [[2019–20 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] in the second round of the [[2020 NBA playoffs]] on September 8, 2020, Herro became the first player in NBA history born in the 2000s to appear in an NBA Conference Finals game.{{cite web |last=Gaydos |first=Ryan |date=September 9, 2020 |title=Heat rookie Tyler Herro will become first person born in the 2000s to make NBA conference finals appearance |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/heat-tyler-herro-born-2000-nba-conference-finals |access-date=September 9, 2020 |work=Fox News}} On September 15, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|2019–20 NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] by the league.{{cite web |date=September 15, 2020 |title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019-20 Kia All-Rookie First Team Tyler Herro, Rui Hachimura voted to Second Team |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release |access-date=September 15, 2020 |website=NBA.com}} In game [[2020 NBA playoffs|4]] of the 2020 Eastern Conference Finals, he scored a career-high 37 points, becoming the fourth player in playoffs history to record 30-plus points before turning 21 and the second-highest scorer under 21, with only [[Magic Johnson]] scoring more.{{Cite web |last=Polockas |first=Erikas |date=September 24, 2020 |title=Tyler Herro joins Magic Johnson and Derrick Rose |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/104815-tyler-herro-joins-magic-johnson-and-derrick-rose |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=TalkBasket.net |language=en}}{{Cite news |last=Golliver |first=Ben |date=September 24, 2020 |title=Analysis {{!}} Tyler Herro had an NBA playoff game for a rookie that compares to only Magic Johnson |language=en-US |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/09/24/tyler-herro-heat-celtics/ |access-date=September 25, 2020 |issn=0190-8286}} He also set Conference Finals records for the youngest player (at 20 years, 247 days old) to score 30-plus points and the most points by a rookie.{{cite web |last=Zillgitt |first=Jeff |date=September 24, 2020 |title=How 20-year-old Heat rookie Tyler Herro sank Celtics in Game 4 of Eastern Conference finals |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/heat/2020/09/23/tyler-herro-14-baskets-game-4-heat-celtics/3514215001/ |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=USA Today}} After an Eastern Conference Finals victory against the [[Boston Celtics]], Herro became the first player born in the 2000s to play in an NBA Finals.{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=September 29, 2020 |title=Tyler Herro hasn't forgotten the 12 players drafted ahead of him |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/09/29/tyler-herro-miami-heat-nba-draft-motivation/ |access-date=September 29, 2020 |website=USA Today}} During game [[2020 NBA Finals#Game 2|2]] of the [[2020 NBA Finals]], Herro became the youngest player to start an NBA Finals game at 20 years, 256 days—eight days younger than Magic Johnson was when he started game 1 for the Lakers in [[1980 NBA Finals|1980]] against the [[1979–80 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=October 3, 2020 |title=Heat's Tyler Herro breaks Magic Johnson's record becoming youngest player ever to start an NBA Finals game |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/heats-tyler-herro-breaks-magic-johnsons-record-becoming-youngest-player-ever-to-start-an-nba-finals-game/#:~:text=NBA%20Schedule-,Heat%27s%20Tyler%20Herro%20breaks%20Magic%20Johnson%27s%20record%20becoming%20youngest%20player,start%20an%20NBA%20Finals%20game |access-date=October 9, 2020 |publisher=cbssports.com}} In [[2020 NBA Finals#Game 4|game 4]] of the same Finals series, he achieved the most three-pointers made by a rookie in [[NBA playoffs]] history, accomplishing 45 three-point shots while surpassing [[Matt Maloney]]'s record 43 threes during the [[1997 NBA playoffs|1997 playoffs]].{{cite web |last=Villanueva |first=Virgil |date=October 6, 2020 |title=Heat's Tyler Herro makes playoffs history with incredible 3-point shooting |url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-tyler-herro-makes-playoffs-history-with-incredible-3-point-shooting/ |access-date=October 10, 2020 |publisher=Clutchpoints.com}} On October 9, 2020, Herro broke a 44-year-old record by scoring 10 points on the third quarter of the [[2020 NBA Finals#Game 5|game 5]] of the [[2020 NBA Finals]]—setting the NBA record by a rookie for the most consecutive games in the playoffs scoring in double digits with 20 while surpassing [[Alvan Adams]]'s record of 19 games of the [[1975–76 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]] in [[1976 NBA playoffs|1976]].{{cite web |date=October 9, 2020 |title=Tyler Herro just set another rookie NBA playoff scoring record |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/10/09/tyler-herro-nba-rookie-playoff-consecutive-scoring-record/ |access-date=October 12, 2020 |publisher=The Rookie Wire}} The Heat lost the series in 6 games to the [[2019–20 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]]. On January 12, 2021, Herro scored a season-high 34 points, alongside seven rebounds and four assists, in a 134–137 overtime loss to the [[2020–21 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=Embiid scores 45, Mathias wins it for 76ers in OT on 3 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000157 |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=NBA}} On February 17, he grabbed a career-high-tying 15 rebounds, alongside 11 points and four assists, in a 112–120 loss to the [[2020–21 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Curry and his supporting cast rally Warriors past Heat in OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000443 |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=NBA}} On May 16, Herro logged a career-high 11 assists, alongside 16 points and six rebounds, in a 120–107 win over the [[2020–21 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |title=Heat rout Pistons 120-107 with several key players out |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022001069 |access-date=May 8, 2022 |website=NBA}} In the [[2021 NBA playoffs|2021 playoffs]], the Heat lost in four games to the eventual champion [[2020–21 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] in the first round. ==== 2021–2023: Sixth Man of the Year and second Finals appearance ==== On October 23, 2021, Herro became the first player in Heat franchise history to record at least 30 points and 10 rebounds off the bench, which he achieved in a 102–91 loss to the [[2021–22 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=Miami Heat vs. Indiana Pacers Box Score, Summary, and Team Stats - October 23, 2021 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/boxscore/NBA_20211023_MIA@IND/ |access-date=October 23, 2021 |website=CBS Sports}} On April 5, 2022, he scored a season-high 35 points, alongside six rebounds and three assists, in a 144–115 win over the [[2021–22 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2022 |title=HERRO SCORES 35, HEAT BEAT HORNETS 144-115 FOR 5TH STRAIGHT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101181 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Herro was named the 2022 [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]], making him the first player in Heat franchise history to win the award.{{Cite web |date=May 4, 2022 |title=Heat's Tyler Herro wins 2021-22 Kia Sixth Man of the Year award |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2021-22-kia-sixth-man-of-the-year |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} During the first round of the playoffs, the Heat eliminated the [[2021–22 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]] in five games. On May 2, 2022, during the Heat's second-round series against the [[2021–22 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]], Herro recorded 25 points and seven assists in a 106–92 game 1 win.{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=May 3, 2022 |title=HERRO SCORES 25, HEAT TAKE GAME 1 OVER 76ERS 106-92 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100201 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Heat defeated the 76ers in six games and advanced to the [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference Finals]], where they faced the [[2021–22 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]]. Herro missed games 3 through 6 of the series with a groin injury.{{Cite web |title=Heat vs. Celtics injury updates: Miami's Tyler Herro returns for Game 7 of Eastern Conference finals |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/heat-vs-celtics-injury-updates-miamis-tyler-herro-returns-for-game-7-of-eastern-conference-finals/ |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=CBS Sports|date=May 29, 2022 }} He returned for game 7, but only played seven minutes as the Heat were eliminated in a 100–96 loss.{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=May 30, 2022 |title=CELTICS REACH NBA FINALS, HOLD OFF HEAT 100-96 IN GAME 7 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100307 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On October 2, 2022, Herro signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension with the Miami Heat.{{Cite web |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Hear Re-sign Tyler Herro |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-tyler-herro-to-an-extension-100222 |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On November 2, Herro put up 26 points alongside a game-winning three in a 110–107 win over the [[2022–23 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last=Salao |first=R.P. |date=November 2, 2022 |title=VIDEO: Tyler Herro stuns Kings with game-winning three |url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-tyler-herro-stuns-kings-with-game-winning-three/ |access-date=November 2, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints}} On November 27, Herro recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a 106–98 victory over the [[2022–23 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2022 |title=Bam Adebayo has 32 points, Heat rally to beat Hawks 106–98 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468448 |access-date=2022-12-02 |website=ESPN.com}} On December 15, Herro put up a career-high 41 points on 10-of-15 shooting from three-point range alongside five rebounds in a 111–108 win over the [[2022–23 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]]. He also became the youngest player in NBA history to put up at least 40 points, 10 three-pointers made and five rebounds in a game.{{cite web |last=Villas |first=Rexwell |date=December 15, 2022 |title=Tyler Herro sets bonkers NBA record after going nuclear vs Rockets |url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-tyler-herro-sets-bonkers-nba-record-after-going-nuclear-vs-rockets |access-date=December 15, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints}} On December 31, Herro put up a buzzer-beating, game-winning three-pointer in a 126–123 win against the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. He finished the game with 29 points, nine rebounds, six assists and two steals.{{cite web |last=Guinhawa |first=Angelo |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Tyler Herro's buzzer-beater vs. Jazz reminds Heat fans of Dwyane Wade |url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-tyler-herro-buzzer-beater-vs-jazz-reminds-miami-fans-of-dwyane-wade |access-date=December 31, 2022 |website=ClutchPoints}}{{cite web |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Herro's 3 as time expires gives Heat 126-123 win over Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468701 |access-date=January 2, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Herro ended the year as league leader in free-throw percentage at 93.4%. Herro broke his right hand in the first round of the 2023 playoffs against the [[2022–23 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]]. He was expected to be out for at least six weeks after undergoing surgery.{{cite news |last=Stinar |first=Ben |title=Significant Miami Heat Player Remains Out Indefinitely |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/injuries/miami-heat-tyler-herro-remains-out-indefinitely-boston-celtics-nba-playoffs |access-date=May 20, 2023 |work=Fastbreak on FanNation |date=May 16, 2023 |language=en}} Even though he became available to play in game 5 of the NBA Finals against the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], the Heat did not play him before losing the game and series to the Nuggets.{{cite news |title=Herro deemed available but still sits out Game 5 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37841322 |access-date=June 23, 2023 |work=ESPN.com |date=June 12, 2023 |language=en}} ==== 2023–2025: First All-Star appearance and Three-Point contest champion ==== On October 30, 2023, Herro scored a season-high 35 points during a 122–114 loss to the Milwaukee Bucks.[https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2023/10/30/milwaukee-bucks-miami-heat-nba-game-score-injury-report-starting-lineup-damian-lillard-jimmy-butler/71379312007/ Giannis, Lillard help Bucks hold off Heat's big rally in fourth quarter, 122-114] On April 24, 2024, in Game 2 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(1) Boston Celtics vs. (8) Miami Heat|First Round]] against the [[Boston Celtics]], Herro put up 24 points, five rebounds and a playoff career-high 14 assists in a 111–101 victory to even the series.{{cite web |title=Herro scores 24, Heat hit franchise playoff-record 23 3s to beat Boston and even series 1-1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401655100 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 28, 2024 |date=April 24, 2024}} Herro's statistics were nearly identical to the previous year during the regular season, but took a noticeable decline in the playoffs. Miami would ultimately lose the series in five games as Boston would go on to be the eventual [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA champions]]. In May, Heat president [[Pat Riley]] labeled Herro as "fragile" during a press conference, referencing the fact that he had missed nearly half of the season due to injuries.{{Cite web |last=Crisafulli |first=Owen |date=2024-05-06 |title=Heat's Pat Riley takes jab at 'fragile' Tyler Herro after another injury-plagued season |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/miami-heat/heat-news-pat-riley-takes-jab-fragile-tyler-herro-another-injury-plagued-season |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=[[ClutchPoints]] |language=en}} On November 12, 2024, Herro scored 40 points and made 10 three-pointers in a 123–121 overtime loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. His 10 three-pointers equaled the Heat franchise record.{{cite news |title=Spoelstra's 'horrendous mistake' mars 40-point game by Herro in Heat loss in Detroit |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article294070944.html |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=miamiherald.com |date=12 November 2024}} On December 29, Herro helped the Heat rally from a 12-point deficit by recording a game-high 27 points, as well as nine assists and six rebounds, in a 104–100 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]]. With 35 seconds left in the game, became entangled with Rockets player [[Amen Thompson]] as the ball was being inbounded before Thompson threw him to the floor. The subsequent altercation resulted in him, Thompson and four other people being ejected.{{Cite web |date=2024-12-30 |title=Amen Thompson-Tyler Herro fight leads to multiple ejections |url=https://www.nba.com/news/amen-thompson-tyler-herro-fight-leads-to-ejections-of-multiple-players-and-coaches-in-heats-victory-in-houston |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=[[NBA]] |language=en |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} By the end of December, Herro was leading the Heat in passes made, assists, potential assists and points via assists during the season, recording career highs in all categories. His efficiency had also increased for numerous shot types and areas as he more frequently attacked the rim rather than attempt long two-pointers.{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=James |date=2025-01-31 |title=Wow, Boy Wonder: How Tyler Herro’s NBA All-Star case grows by the day |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6026899/2024/12/30/tyler-herro-heat-all-star-nba/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} By mid-January, Herro was "not only been the Heat’s most available player this season, he’s also been the team’s most reliable and best source of offense" while averaging his best season to date according to the [[Miami Herald|''Miami Herald'']].{{Cite web |last=Chiang |first=Anthony |date=2025-01-14 |title=Once labeled as ‘fragile,’ Tyler Herro changing narratives around him. Also, Heat injury updates |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article298490363.html |access-date=2025-04-23 |website=[[Miami Herald]]}} On January 30, 2025, Herro was named as a reserve player for the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game]], his first selection.{{cite web| title= Victor Wembanyama, Jaylen Brown highlight 2025 All-Star Game reserves | website=NBA.com | date=January 30, 2025 | url= https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-all-star-game-reserves | access-date=February 2, 2025}} On February 15, Herro won the NBA [[Three-Point Contest]] in [[San Francisco]], defeating [[Buddy Hield]] and [[Darius Garland]] in the final round.{{cite web |title=Miami Heat star Tyler Herro wins 2025 Starry 3-Point Contest |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-3-point-contest |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 16, 2025}} With the departure of [[Jimmy Butler]] in February 2025, Herro was seen as the most probable successor to leading the team through the post-season. On April 1, Herro recorded 25 points and nine assists in a 124–103 win over the Boston Celtics.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-04-02 |title=Tyler Herro helps Miami Heat snap Boston Celtics' nine-game win streak |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/tyler-herro-helps-miami-heat-snap-boston-celtics-nine-game-win-streak-1.2281376 |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |language=en-CA |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}} On April 16, Herro scored 38 points, the most ever scored by a single Heat player in a play-in game, during a 109–90 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite news |last=Weiss |first=Jared |date=2025-04-18 |title=Playoff Herro was leader Heat needed to dismantle Bulls, advance in Play-In Tournament |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6286219/2025/04/17/tyler-herro-heat-leader-play-in-tournament/ |access-date=2025-04-19 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} On April 18, Herro scored 30 points, including two three-pointers in overtime, during a 123–114 win against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the play-in.{{Cite web |last=Odum |first=Charles |date=2025-04-19 |title=Herro scores 30 points to lead Heat past Hawks 123-114 in OT in play-in and into NBA playoffs |url=https://apnews.com/article/heat-hawks-score-playin-ea7ed0a265e23b3f852457b814c5fe53 |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=[[AP News]] |language=en}} The win allowed the Heat to become the first tenth seed team to clinch a playoff appearance.{{Cite web |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |date=2025-04-18 |title=Heat a perfect 10, beat Hawks in OT. But do they have enough depth to beat 64-win Cavs? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2025/04/18/heat-hawks-nba-play-in-tournament/83168285007/ |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=[[USA TODAY]] |language=en-US}} On April 23, in game 2 of the first round of the playoffs, Herro scored 33 points in a 112–121 loss against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |last=Reedy |first=Joe |date=2025-04-24 |title=Mitchell scores 30 points, Cavaliers hold off Heat 121-112 to take 2-0 lead in NBA playoff series |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-playoffs-2025-heat-cavaliers-da7143692335069076c0c693a75fbf59 |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=[[AP News]] |language=en}} Herro scored only four points on 1-of-10 shooting in a 138–83 blowout loss to the Cavaliers in game 4, completing the four-game sweep and eliminating the Heat.{{Cite web |last=Chiang |first=Anthony |date=2025-04-28 |title=Heat’s season ends with first-round sweep to Cavs in historically bad loss. In turn, Herro also portrayed himself in the [[White Men Can't Jump (2023 film)|''White Men Can't Jump'' remake]] starring Harlow.{{Cite web|last=Harlow|first=Jack|date=October 22, 2020|title=Jack Harlow Music video "Tyler Herro"|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=np9Ub1LilKU&list=TLPQMjgxMDIwMjB0veiwtSF8Gg&index=2|access-date=October 28, 2020|website=YouTube}} In 2020, Herro began dating Katya Elise Henry.{{ Cite web | title=@nolimitherro|date=November 26, 2020|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CIEdYjljQCE/?igshid=1nxjy6tbpomql |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/CIEdYjljQCE |archive-date=2021-12-24 |url-access=limited|website=Instagram}}{{cbignore}} On June 5, 2021, they announced that they were expecting a child.{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/sports/tyler-herro-katya-elise-henry-pregnancy|title= Tyler Herro Expecting Baby With Girlfriend Katya Elise Henry|work=Complex|date=June 5, 2021|last=Cummings-Grady|first=Mackenzie}} Their daughter was born on September 14, 2021.{{cite web | last=Richardson | first=Shandel | title=Miami Heat's Tyler Herro Matures After Birth of Daughter | website=SI.com | date=2021-09-24 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/heat/miami-news/miami-heat-tyler-herro-maturity | access-date=2025-02-17}} On June 18, 2022, the couple announced that they were expecting a second child.{{cite web | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Ce9m6mPuGMc/ | title=Instagram }} Their son was born on January 12, 2023.{{Cite web |last=Andaloro |first=Angela |date=2023-01-12 |title=Miami Heat's Tyler Herro and Girlfriend Katya Henry Welcome Baby No. 2 — See the Photo!
